newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares lead in Beirut weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares lead in Beirut weekly trade.

text.p: Bank shares steamed ahead "in healthy trade" on the Beirut Stock Exchange during the week ending on Friday and brokers said the stocks were expected to rise further.
"The trend will stay up because the banks' fundamentals are very good," Nicholas Sawan, Deputy Manager head of tranding at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said.
Banque Audi touched an alltime high of $23.125 on Friday from $23 last week. It fell on Tuesday to $22.25 only to pick up again towards the end of the week.
"An important point to stress is the fact that the shares have been able to go up and down in the past two weeks," Sawan told Reuters.
"Market makers are becoming flexible enough to allow the shares to fluctuate naturally. This is a healthy sign," he said.
Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce touched during the week a record $17.75. It fell back to $17.625 on Friday, well above last week's closing at $16.5.
Bank of Beirut rose to $3.6875 from $3.5625 last week. Four block trades totalling 75,000 shares traded at between $3.5625 and $3.6875 on the floor.
A little less than 60,000 Audi shares were traded in a block at $22.25 on the BSE during the week. A block of 30,000 shares traded at $22.25 off the floor.
Seven BLC block trades totalling 42,500 shares traded on the BSE during the week at prices ranging between $16.75 and $17.625. One block of 15,000 shares traded off the bourse.
The LIBX bank index rose 3.59 percent on the week to 149.13. The LISPI general index fell 0.13 percent to 88.42 while the BLOM general index rose 0.04 percent to 930.88.

Solidere shares were unchanged from last week. A traded at $10.5 on Friday while B shares traded at $10.75. Demand for the shares was strengthening throughout the week and brokers said the stock was expected to rise next week.
"It's logical. Downside is limited, almost nonexistent for Solidere now," Sawan said.

Of the four industrial shares, pipemaker Eternit fell to $1.9375 from $2 while Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.28125. Ciments Blancs, which last traded on Thursday at $4.75 was down from $5.1875 a week earlier.
There was no trade in either tilemaker Uniceramic throughout the week.
Total BSE turnover was 1,074,511 shares for a value of $11,467,988 from last week's turnover of 929,740 shares for $7,571,492.
